name: com.modelread/modelread
title: modelread
description: Will this Hugging Face model run on my hardware? Fit, best quant, tok/s range, launch command.

tools.name: estimate_fit
tools.description: Will this Hugging Face repo run on this hardware? Checks the repo and its quantized derivatives (GGUF/MLX/AWQ...) and returns, per candidate: verdict (fits | fits-tight | offload | no | unknown), memory placement (VRAM / RAM / SSD), longest context that fits, decode and prefill tok/s bands with basis, concurrent-serving aggregate, runtime support (llama.cpp / vLLM / MLX registries) and an exact launch command. repo: 'org/name' (base model or a GGUF repo). hardware: preset id, '<N>x-<id>', free text, or 'gpu=..,ram=..,bw=..'; pass the usable memory the user states: 'jetson-thor,usable=117'. ctx in tokens. When nothing is recommended, memory_check lists each quant's need in GiB and whether it fits in memory. If the repo is not on the Hub the result is error 'model_not_found' with a message and no estimate. model.license and model.native_ctx (the model's own context limit) come with it. variant: only this quant, e.g. 'Q8_0' (default: the best for the device). response_format: leave unset; the default has every decision field in <2k tokens. 'detailed' adds only the best candidate's files, notes and source URLs.

tools.name: compare_hardware
tools.description: Run one repo against several devices and return the best candidate per device (verdict, quant, decode band, max context, launch command), sorted best first. When devices get different quants (so their speeds are not comparable), same_quant names one file that runs on all of them and each row's same_quant has its speed there. Use for 'which of my machines should run X' or 'is a 4090 or an M4 Max better for X'. hardware: comma-separated list of presets / free text / custom specs, e.g. 'rtx3090, unified=1,ram=96,bw=256' is two devices; ';' also separates devices (max 8).

tools.name: find_models
tools.description: Recommend models for a task on given hardware, written as a natural question, e.g. 'best coding model for an RTX 4090 + 64GB RAM at 32k context', 'Japanese chat on a Galaxy S25 Ultra', 'serve 8 users on 2x RTX 3090'. Ranks indexed Hub models (~20k, refreshed nightly) by fit, task benchmark percentile (provenance-tagged, vendor vs independent), speed and adoption; each result carries a fit estimate and its release date (response_format: leave unset). Keep a release window in the question ('released in the last two months', 'since October 2026'): rows are then filtered or marked in_window, and the answer says when nothing inside it qualifies. Tasks understood: chat, coding, agentic, vision, ocr, math, reasoning, multilingual, function-calling, embedding, reranking, speech-to-text, tts, image-generation, video-generation.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Free-form question about running Hugging Face models locally or self-hosted (runtimes, quant choice, KV cache, why something OOMs, MoE offload); returns markdown plus the parsed query and notes.

tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Search the model index by name without estimating (fast): ids, task, library, params, downloads, likes, license, created date, gated. query: words that must all appear in the repo id, any order, case-insensitive, '-_.' optional; family, uploader, quant method or org/name all work ('qwen3', 'gemma-4', 'ubergarm', 'qwen3.8 nvfp4', 'Flash-Next-GGUF'), quantized derivatives included. Only matching repos are returned: an empty list means no indexed repo has that name (drop a word to widen; a repo missing here may still exist on the Hub). not_on_hub: indexed earlier, since removed or private. task: any|chat|coding|vision|ocr|embedding|speech-to-text|tts|image-generation|video-generation|robotics or a Hub pipeline tag (default: any with a query, chat without); max_params_billion filters by size. About 40 rows fit one result; offset pages.

tools.name: list_hardware
tools.description: List hardware presets (330+: GPUs of every vendor and segment, multi-GPU nodes, Apple, Jetson/APUs, phones, tablets, SBCs, VPS tiers). filter: words matched against id/name/vendor/segment, e.g. 'h100', 'amd datacenter', 'phone samsung', 'vps'. Returns id, name, kind, memory, bandwidth, backend; offset pages.
